questions.questionHTML: According to the passage on Global Supply Chain Resilience, what factor predominantly disrupted the traditional "just-in-time" inventory model?
questions.passageHTML:
Global Supply Chain Resilience and the "China+1" Paradigm

The geopolitical frictions and catastrophic logistical bottlenecks of recent years have precipitated a fundamental restructuring of multinational production networks. For decades, multinational corporations operated under hyper-optimized "just-in-time" inventory models concentrated overwhelmingly in single geographic regions to minimize unit manufacturing costs. However, systemic supply disruptions underscored the catastrophic vulnerability of such concentrated supply chains, catalyzing a strategic pivot toward "just-in-case" resilience and geographic diversification.

India’s flagship Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes across key sectors—including telecommunications, electronics, high-efficiency solar photovoltaic modules, and advanced chemistry cell batteries—are calibrated directly to capture this structural redistribution of manufacturing capacity. By providing substantial fiscal incentives on incremental sales, the PLI scheme has successfully attracted global contract manufacturers and stimulated domestic capital expenditure. Yet, to achieve enduring global competitiveness, India must concurrently address foundational structural bottlenecks: reducing elevated logistics costs (which currently hover near 13-14% of GDP compared to 8% in developed economies), accelerating port turnaround timelines, and harmonizing state-level labor regulations.

questions.questionHTML: Question 31: A train 240 meters long crosses a platform of equal length in 24 seconds. Find the speed of the train in km/h.
questions.explanationHTML:
Total distance = 240 + 240 = 480 meters. Speed = 480 / 24 = 20 m/s.
In km/h = 20 * (18 / 5) = 72 km/h.
